Independently re-verify this claim yourself against the actual current code -- do not just trust the summary; specifically try struct values (DateTime.utc_now(), URI.parse(...), MapSet.new([1]), 1..5) against metadata AND at least 2 other attrs fields yourself. This is the third INV-8 pass on this run (2 prior FAILs, same invariant) -- if you find yet another crash, treat it seriously; if genuinely clean this time, don't manufacture a reason to fail. Re-run the full INV-1..INV-8 gate fresh -- do not just re-check INV-8, confirm INV-1/INV-7 still hold against the new diff too (fetch_event_type/1 is new code you haven't reviewed yet). result.summary:
THIRD pass on this run's INV-8 check. Re-ran the full INV-1..INV-8 gate fresh against `git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/event_store.ex lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex` (622-line diff, read in full end to end, not just the fix hunk), plus independent empirical verification against the real compiled app via `mix compile --force` (clean) and `mix run scratch/verify_inv8_req025_pass3.exs` -- not a re-implementation of the logic in isolation, the actual `Letflow.EventStore.append/2` and `Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1` public entry points.

Scope test: append/2 writes tenant-scoped rows across events, instance_sequence, instance_projections, event_payload_store, event_idempotency, deriving tenant_id from opts[:prefix] rather than accepting it from attrs; tenant_provisioning.ex adds tenant_id_for_schema_name/1, the reverse-derivation function this depends on. IN SCOPE (tenant-data path).

INV-1 (tenant isolation) -- APPLIES, PASS. (a) Every Repo/Multi call site in event_store.ex passes `prefix: schema_name` -- re-read all sites (active_instance_guard's repo.get, assign_sequence's insert + FOR-UPDATE repo.one + repo.update_all, claim_idempotency's insert/repo.get/repo.get_by, insert_event, store_oversized_payload, update_projection) -- unchanged, all present. (b) `reject_tenant_id/1` rejects both atom `:tenant_id` and string `"tenant_id"` keys with `{:error, :tenant_id_not_accepted}` before anything else runs. Verified empirically, not just from prose: called `Letflow.EventStore.append/2` with a real valid prefix (`tenant_bbbb...b`, whose genuine derived tenant_id is `bbbbbbbb-bbbb-...`) and attrs carrying an attacker-supplied *mismatched* tenant_id (both atom-keyed `11111111-...` and string-keyed `22222222-...`) -- both calls returned `{:error, :tenant_id_not_accepted}`, confirming the rejection is unconditional (never a compare-and-allow-if-matching branch, which would be a weaker and error-prone design). (c) `tenant_id_for_schema_name/1` cannot derive a wrong tenant: its second function clause (`def tenant_id_for_schema_name(_schema_name), do: {:error, :invalid_schema_name}`, guarding the is_binary/1-guarded first clause) means any non-binary input falls straight to the terminal error, never a partial/lossy match. Verified empirically against 6 probe values including a SQL-metacharacter payload (`nil`, `:an_atom`, `123`, `"unrelated"`, `"tenant_'; DROP TABLE events; --"`, and a 32-char-but-non-hex string `tenant_gggg...g`) -- all six returned `{:error, :invalid_schema_name}`, none crashed, none produced a tenant_id, none reached SQL (the function is pure -- no Repo call anywhere in its body). Since append/2's `with` chain calls `tenant_id_for_schema_name(prefix)` before ctx is built and before any Repo call uses `prefix: schema_name`, a prefix that fails this check never reaches a query -- the attribution-integrity mechanism the 0003 addendum specifies holds end to end.

INV-2/INV-3/INV-5 -- NOT-APPLICABLE, unchanged (no API/response-shaping code, no scripting sandbox, no lookup-by-ID endpoint; S4/S5 not started).

INV-4 (secrets) -- NOT-APPLICABLE to this diff's content: `grep -niE "password|secret|token|api_key|System.get_env" lib/letflow/event_store.ex lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex` -- zero hits.

INV-6 -- APPLIES, satisfied by this handoff's explicit per-invariant statement (this document).

INV-7 (no raw SQL string interpolation) -- APPLIES, PASS. `grep -n "Repo\.query\|fragment(" lib/letflow/event_store.ex lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex` -- zero hits in event_store.ex; `lock_and_increment_sequence/3`'s FOR-UPDATE read composes `InstanceSequence |> where([s], s.instance_id == ^instance_id) |> lock("FOR UPDATE") |> repo.one(prefix: schema_name)` -- a pinned bind param via Ecto's query API, not a string. tenant_provisioning.ex's two `Repo.query!` calls (advisory lock with a genuine `$1` bind param; `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS "#{schema_name}"` identifier interpolation) are pre-existing, untouched by this diff's added lines (confirmed against the diff hunks -- only `+` lines touch tenant_provisioning.ex, no `-` lines near those calls), and schema_name there is still only ever `schema_name_for_tenant/1`'s constrained `tenant_[0-9a-f]{32}` output, not raw external input -- consistent with the prior pass. The new `tenant_id_for_schema_name/1` performs zero SQL (pure string/regex/`Ecto.UUID.cast`), so it cannot be an injection vector regardless of input -- empirically confirmed above (the SQL-metacharacter payload never reached a query).

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES, PASS. This is the specific claim under re-verification: ELIXIR-DEV changed `validate_metadata/1`'s guard to `when not is_map(metadata) or is_struct(metadata)` and reported the rest of the pre-transaction phase (fetch_uuid/3, fetch_payload/1, fetch_idempotency_key/1, fetch_event_type/1) already safe against struct-shaped input. Independently verified, not trusted: wrote scratch/verify_inv8_req025_pass3.exs and ran it via `mix run` against the real compiled app (`mix compile --force` succeeded clean first). Tested 4 struct types (`DateTime.utc_now()`, `URI.parse("http://x")`, `MapSet.new([1,2,3])`, `1..5` (Range)) against `metadata` AND FIVE other attrs fields (`instance_id`, `actor_id`, `payload`, `idempotency_key`, `event_type` -- exceeding the 'at least 2 other fields' bar), 24 total struct-value calls into the real `Letflow.EventStore.append/2`. Result: zero crashes across all 24. metadata -> `{:error, {:invalid_metadata, :not_a_map}}` for all 4 (confirms the new `is_struct(metadata)` guard clause actually fires and wins before the second `map_size/1` clause or the `Enum.find_value/3` body ever run -- a struct is a map under the hood so `map_size/1` would not itself have crashed, but iteration inside the old body previously did; the guard now intercepts before either). instance_id/actor_id -> `{:error, :missing_instance_id}`/`{:error, :missing_actor_id}` for all 4 each (`fetch_uuid/3`'s `Ecto.UUID.cast/1` returns `:error` for non-binary struct input rather than raising -- confirmed, not assumed). payload -> `{:error, :missing_payload}` for all 4 (`is_binary/1` guard in `fetch_payload/1` safely evaluates false on a struct, no crash). idempotency_key -> `{:error, :missing_idempotency_key}` for all 4 (same `is_binary/1` pattern in `fetch_idempotency_key/1`). event_type -> `{:error, :missing_event_type}` for all 4 (same `is_binary/1` pattern in `fetch_event_type/1`, the function added in the prior rework iteration to close the `Registry.get_type/2` Ecto-query crash -- re-confirmed safe against structs specifically, not just against the nil/atom/integer shapes it was built for). The `^\s*{:ok, .*} = ` heuristic grep found 3 hits, all manually confirmed to be `case`/`with`-branch patterns inside `->`, not bare match-or-raise assignments -- false positives, not violations. Verdict: the rework's fix is genuine and complete for every pre-transaction field this reviewer could construct a struct-shaped attack against; no new crash found this pass.

Regarding this handoff's specific check (c) (could metadata validation be bypassed to smuggle oversized/malicious data into jsonb): still no -- for any input that survives validation without crashing (plain maps with string keys/values), the entry-count/key-length/value-length checks in `validate_metadata/1`'s final clause are sound and unbypassable, unchanged from prior passes; the struct-shaped crash class was availability (INV-8), never a data-integrity bypass (INV-1) or injection (INV-7).

Overall: all applicable invariants (INV-1, INV-4 N/A, INV-6, INV-7, INV-8) PASS. This is genuinely clean -- no new finding manufactured to avoid a third consecutive rubber-stamp-looking PASS; the two prior FAILs were real (raise-on-malformed-input, then the struct-shaped gap in the first fix attempt) and this iteration's fix closes the gap the second FAIL identified, verified independently rather than trusted.
